content.title: What is PreparedStatement?
content.description: PreparedStatement is a JDBC interface used to execute precompiled, parameterized SQL statements. It improves performance, enhances security, and helps prevent SQL Injection attacks.

content.content: PreparedStatement extends the Statement interface by allowing SQL queries to contain placeholders (?) for parameters. These parameters are supplied separately before execution, making the code safer, easier to maintain, and more efficient when the same query is executed multiple times.

content.title: Why Use PreparedStatement?
content.content: PreparedStatement prevents SQL Injection, supports parameterized queries, improves performance through query precompilation, and makes SQL statements easier to read and maintain.
A PreparedStatement object is created using the prepareStatement() method of the Connection interface.

content.title: Creating a PreparedStatement
content.code:
String sql = "SELECT * FROM students WHERE id = ?";
PreparedStatement ps = con.prepareStatement(sql);

content.title: Key Idea
content.description: SQL is compiled once and reused multiple times with different parameter values, improving efficiency.

content.content: Parameter values are assigned using setter methods such as setInt(), setString(), setDouble(), and setDate().
PreparedStatement supports executing SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE statements using dedicated execution methods.

content.title: Preprinted Application Form
content.content: Imagine a printed application form with blank spaces. The form structure remains the same, while only the values are filled in for each applicant. PreparedStatement works similarly by preparing the SQL once and filling different parameter values each time.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: PreparedStatement, SQL Injection prevention, parameterized queries, executeQuery(), executeUpdate(), placeholders (?), JDBC transactions, and Statement vs PreparedStatement comparisons are among the most commonly asked Java interview topics.

items.question: Why shouldn't user input be concatenated into SQL?
items.answer: String concatenation can make applications vulnerable to SQL Injection attacks.

items.question: Must every placeholder receive a value?
items.answer: Yes. Every '?' placeholder must be assigned a value before execution.

items.question: Should PreparedStatement be reused?
items.answer: Yes. Reusing a PreparedStatement for repeated executions improves performance.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: PreparedStatement is the preferred JDBC interface for executing parameterized SQL queries because it is secure, efficient, and easy to maintain.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Values are assigned using setter methods.
PreparedStatement is preferred over Statement in most applications.
